===== CLAUDE.md =====

# flyee.club — Platform monorepo

The PLATFORM of flyee.club: accounts, billing (Asaas for BRL, Stripe for USD, and Stripe for BRL too until Asaas is set up), entitlements, member token issuance with 30-day revalidation, the package-delivery API the `npx flyee` CLI consumes, catalog and release management, the member dashboard, admin consoles, per-segment metrics, the waitlist and the bilingual public site. The PRODUCT (the CLI, the harness core and the module contents) is a separate project that consumes this platform's API contract and module manifest; it never lives here. This repo has no link to any template: it was copied from the MedChina codebase on 2026-09-30 and is being reshaped into the platform phase by phase.

## Safety during the transition

- `apps/web/.env` was inherited with **MedChina production credentials** (Supabase, Asaas, Meta, GA4, AI keys), and `apps/web/.env.local` was created on 2026-09-30 to blank every one of them. Since 2026-10-14 the remote database scripts have run against the hosted flyee.club project (`bb2e934`, `e09cf08`), which `docs/DEPLOY.md` allows only once the local files hold its values: they now carry flyee.club production credentials, the service role key included, and may still carry MedChina's. Never open, print or copy either file, and never write to the hosted database without the operator's yes. Next.js loads `.env.local` first, so a value there wins. A key the inherited file defines and `.env.local` does not is still read from the copy: `npm run preflight` names each one, and never prints a value.
- Never run `db:plan:remote`, `db:migrate:remote`, `db:gate:remote` or `test:db:remote` until `.env.local` points at the new flyee.club Supabase project. The gate (`scripts/remote-db-gate.mjs`) reads `.env.local` first, bootstraps an EMPTY project, and refuses a database it did not build (the MedChina one included, whose history names files this repo does not have), but do not lean on that.
- Never commit `.env`, `.env.local` or any other env file: `.gitignore` lists `.env` and `.env.*`, with `.env.example` as the one tracked reference. `.vercelignore`, at the root and in `apps/web`, lists the same two, because the Vercel CLI never reads `.gitignore` and a `vercel deploy` typed on a developer's machine would upload the inherited `apps/web/.env`. The deploy leaves only through the pipeline. Commit per plan phase, never push without being asked.

## Product (summary of docs/PRODUCT.md)

- **What it is**: a club called FlyeeClub, sold as a one-time access (the plan called "FlyeeClub") plus a subscription ("FlyeeClub Pro"). Members install the flyee harness in the AI they already use (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor) and keep receiving versioned tool modules and the updates that keep them working when the AIs change. The club never spends AI credit on the member's behalf.
- **Ladder** (prices are hypotheses stored as data in `plans`, never in code): the free rung (an account with no purchase, reached only through content; it installs the entry version of each app and is never sold or advertised) → FlyeeClub (tier `kit`: one-time, a year of catalog and updates counted from the paid invoice, renewed by buying again, card installments in BRL through Asaas, 1 device; what every CTA sells) → FlyeeClub Pro (tier `club`: monthly or annual: advanced lessons, recipes, meetings, roadmap vote, the "open the hood" depth, 3 devices) → mentoring and consulting, sold on demand through the contact form, never as plans. The former Pro family (`pro-*`) is inactive since migration 0025, kept for history. Every paid plan may be used in client projects; refunds go through support.
- **Delivery**: every plan also has one Claude Code session in the cloud, out of the device ceiling: the newest cloud session takes the place of the previous one and never a computer's (`plans.limits.cloud_sessions`, migration 0044, decided 2026-10-20). The dashboard issues the member token; `npx flyee` installs and updates from the platform's package server. Every update rotates the token; after 30 days without an update the member revalidates in the dashboard, which is where the next tier is offered. Installed tools keep working when access ends; only updates stop.
- **The member never uses the terminal** (decided 2026-10-08, built in 12.6): their AI runs every flyee command, and they only confirm in the conversation, approve the login in the browser and paste keys into a page the CLI opens. Where a screen or an e-mail needs something installed, it gives a sentence to paste into the conversation with the AI ("Instale o flyee seguindo flyee.club/instalar.md"), and the command appears beside it only as a reference. `/instalar.md` (`/en/install.md`) is the plain-Markdown page the AI follows: its text lives in the code, in both languages (`apps/web/src/lib/install-guide.ts`), with every command written the way one run by an AI needs it (`docs/CLI-CONTRACT.md`, 8.2).
- **Catalog**: one icon per module, filtered by seven stages (Planejar, Construir, Publicar, Divulgar, Vender, Escalar, Manter). The public store (the home and `/catalogo`) filters by store categories instead, the kinds of work of the home brief (Vender, Divulgar, Vídeo, Pesquisa, Construir): data edited in `/admin/catalogo` (`catalog_store_categories`, migration 0029), never in a manifest. The member area, the roadmap, the broad-use rule and the CLI API stay on the stages. Example: the video-editing app is in the stage Divulgar and the category Vídeo. Each app also carries the personas it is a good start for (`catalog_modules.personas`, migration 0032, marked in the console): the home brief's "Para quem é" block shows up to three published apps per persona (`lib/catalog/starters.ts`). Each module page carries a written guide in pt-BR and EN (how to use it, and the "open the hood" depth for FlyeeClub Pro), shipped inside each version's package at `guides/<pt-BR|en>/<usar|abrir-o-capo>.md` and shown for the version the member has installed, with an optional short video (unlisted YouTube); plus versions, changelog, declared permissions and checksum. Each app also carries its example of answering a request (`catalog_modules.showcase`, migration 0043, per language), written by the product and sent in its index: the home, `/catalogo` and each app page show the app answering it, never the command that installs it (decided 2026-10-17).
- **Metrics**: usage events only, never content, dimensioned by segment (`negocio`, `agencia`, `produto`, `dev`, `outro`: the public site's personas plus "other", migration 0028), AI tool and language. The focus segment is chosen by a data rule, not a date.
- **Free rung by version** (decided 2026-10-06, built in 12.5 on 2026-10-08 with one rule, option 1): entitlement is per version through channels (`@flyee/catalog/channels`, migration 0040). The free plan is on channel `free` and gets only the entry version of each app (`catalog_module_versions.is_entry`): the first published one takes the mark, the operator moves or clears it in `/admin/catalogo`, and a marked version is not yanked until the mark leaves it. Kit, membership and Pro stay on `latest`; the channel merges as a right, so the widest live source wins. The entry version is never updated because no new version enters `free`, not because of a block. The catalog answers `latest` per channel and `newest` for everyone, so the distance is visible in the CLI and in the dashboard. The module-wide free sample (`is_free_sample`) left the platform; the CLI API keeps the field, always false, because the CLI 1.x declares it.
- **FlyeeClub Pro is offered only inside** (decided 2026-10-08, phase 12: the public site's part is built since 12.2, the member area's since 12.4, `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`, "FlyeeClub Pro on the click"). The public site exists to sell FlyeeClub, the cheap one-time access: no public page names FlyeeClub Pro, shows its price or describes a feature only Pro has (recipes, meetings, proposing and voting, advanced guides, more computers), with or without a lock; `/planos` stays, with one plan; the terms of use keep describing both plans because they are the contract. Inside the member area Pro is offered on the click of a Pro feature, through one upgrade prompt, and a Pro control is never shown disabled. Unprompted, a FlyeeClub member sees it only on the home when use is broad (three or more stages in 30 days) and on the 30-day revalidation screen; an account with no purchase sees both offers, FlyeeClub ("Assinar", the current versions of the apps) and Pro, and keeps the Pro areas in its menu. A Pro area with nothing published, and an app that is planned but not built yet, carry the badge "Em breve". The founders offer was a MedChina concept and left the platform in 12.3 (migration 0038): no page shows a seats counter or a deadline.
- **The product repo** is `C:\AppsProjects\flyee`: the public npm package `flyee` (the CLI; 1.x supersedes an unrelated 0.7.x line the operator owns), the harness core bundled in it, and the apps, which are ZIPs uploaded to this platform, never npm packages. Its canonical harness file is `AGENTS.md` with `CLAUDE.md`/`GEMINI.md` pointers, and skills in `.agents/skills` bridged into `.claude/skills`. The first app is a video-editing app. On 2026-10-08 it held a finished, unpublished CLI 1.x, core 1.2.0 and five built packages (`video-analysis`, `video-render`, `video-studio`, `motion-carousel` 1.0.0 as the entry version and 1.1.0), all accepted by this platform's upload inspection; `docs/PLANO-IMPLEMENTACAO.md`, phase 12, lists what it still needs from here and what this platform asks of it. Another session works there: read it, never edit it.
- **Pipelines, compatibility and the MCP door** (decided 2026-10-06, phase 10, not built): a `workflow` app is a packaged pipeline whose automatic half runs locally without approvals and whose on-demand half takes the decisions; the platform never runs anything. The core keeps a declarative registry of AI tools with two tiers, "tested" (`compatible_ais`) and "compatible by the standard" (`AGENTS.md` + `.agents/skills`, reported as `other`, promoted by data). Every app ships an eval that also runs as a nightly canary. A read-only remote MCP server on the platform and a local one in the CLI are planned. Anti-resale (confirmed 2026-10-06): a signed per-download license binds the harness to the account and machine, generated files carry an opaque account mark, downloads are watched for anomalies, and the terms forbid redistribution; skills are never encrypted and installed apps never stop working.

## Structure

- `apps/web` — Next.js 15 (App Router) + React 19 + MUI v9 + MUI X (the free packages only) + Tailwind 4, deployed on Vercel. See `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`.
  - **Member dashboard** (`app/(dashboard)`): `/inicio` (the member's rung, the install block with machines and the revalidation date, the activation checklist, latest releases, an offer when `lib/upsell.ts` says so), `/modulos` and `/modulos/[slug]` (the catalog, lessons, permissions, releases), `/receitas`, `/novidades`, `/encontros`, `/roadmap` (the votes, the proposals of FlyeeClub Pro members into a queue the operator reviews, the month's most voted idea, and the contact route for a commissioned app), `/settings` (profile, segment, AI tool, language, security and 2FA, devices, billing), plus the three-step wizard at `/onboarding`. Each screen is a server page that loads data with the member's session (`lib/member/*`) and a view that takes plain props. Screens are goal-first, never CRUD by default; quality is enforced by the `product-screen` skill (loaded by `.claude/hooks/product-screen-guard.mjs`, which also injects `components/product/catalog.json`), the `product-lint` hook and the `product-verify` skill.
  - **Admin** (`app/(dashboard)/admin`, superadmin only): overview; the club's consoles — `/admin/membros` (accounts, rungs, machines, the dossier and every action on an account), `/admin/metricas` (the five focus metrics per segment and week, the focus rule, entry doors), `/admin/catalogo` (tools, version upload and publishing, lessons, recipes, trails, delivery settings), `/admin/roadmap` (the queue under review, the month's leader to plan), `/admin/encontros`, `/admin/leads`; then billing, AI model prices, audit, insights, backups, announcements, help, blog and news, site and support. Each console is a server page that reads with the operator's session (`lib/admin/*`, `loadConsole`) and a client view; writes are server actions that check the role again and audit. A Monday digest (`lib/admin-jobs.ts`) rings and e-mails the operators. Admin copy is hardcoded pt-BR.
  - **Public site** (`app/[locale]/(marketing)`): the home, `/como-funciona`, `/catalogo` and `/catalogo/[slug]` (published modules, read-only), `/planos`, `/sobre`, `/contato`, `/ajuda`, `/blog`, the waitlist (`/espera`), the checksum page (`/verificar/[ref]`) and the legal pages rendered from `consent_terms`, composed from `components/marketing/*`, in Portuguese at `/` and in English at `/en` with translated addresses (`src/i18n/routing.ts`). One public address is not a page: `/instalar.md` (`app/[locale]/instalar.md/route.ts`) answers the Markdown a member's AI reads, declared in `routing.ts` like a page, `noindex`, out of the sitemap and never counted as a visit. Campaign pages without the site menu live in `app/[locale]/(funil)` (`noindex`; none today, since the founders offer left). Until the launch stage is `open`, every primary CTA leads to the waitlist and no public text names `/instalar.md` (`invitesToInstall`); once open, a CTA leads to the sign-up and from it straight to the FlyeeClub checkout (`primaryCtaFor` in `lib/launch.ts`), never to the onboarding first. Pricing lists only the plans marked `listed_on_site` in `plans` (FlyeeClub). Every number on a public page comes from the database. The public site renders without MUI (the public shell: `components/site/*`, `style/base.css`, decided 2026-10-07 for the phone score); the signed-in areas mount `components/layout/app-shell.tsx` in their layouts, with MUI and `style/app.css`. Quality is enforced by the `marketing-page` skill (loaded by `.claude/hooks/marketing-guard.mjs`) and the `marketing-lint` hook, both covering the two groups.
  - **Checkout and auth**: `/assinatura`, `/auth/*`, billing webhooks at `/api/webhooks/[provider]`.
  - **CLI connection and delivery** (`docs/CLI-CONTRACT.md`): the OAuth 2.1 server for the first-party `flyee-cli` client (`/oauth/authorize` with its revalidation variant, `/ativar` for device codes, `/revalidar`, `/api/oauth/{token,device,revoke}`), the delivery API `/api/cli/*` (every call walks `lib/cli/gates.ts`: token → scope → entitlement → device → rate), the package upload `/api/admin/catalog/{uploads,versions}` and, for the product's CI with the service token `FLYEE_SERVICE_TOKEN`, `/api/service/catalog/{import,uploads,versions}`, the public checksum page `/verificar/[ref]` and `/instalar.md`, the CLI's front door.
- `packages/design-tokens` — design system source of truth: the palette in `css/yellow.css` (`theme-yellow`: the yellow of the logo, with `--primary-contrast` for a label on it and `--primary-ink` for the primary as a foreground), neutrals and the deep band (`--background-deep`) in `css/common.css`, `css/marketing.css` (fluid display scale, section rhythm, motion). See its README.
- `packages/db` — the SQL baseline with RLS on every table and explicit grants (one organization per member: the personal workspace), the pgTAP suite, and a Drizzle mirror generated from the migrations. See its README.
- `packages/auth` — Supabase clients (browser/server/middleware/service), 2FA step-up, and the parallel session cookie used by support impersonation.
- `packages/billing` — the ladder (the kit as a one-time access purchase; membership and Pro, monthly and yearly; every plan in BRL and in USD), subscriptions with price snapshots, entitlement grants, coupons, invoices; Asaas (BRL) and Stripe (USD) behind one `PaymentProvider`, routed by the plan's currency; `BILLING_BRL_PROVIDER=stripe` sends BRL to Stripe as well. Pure, client-safe helpers in `@flyee/billing/currency` and `@flyee/billing/entitlements`. See `docs/BILLING.md`.
- `packages/email` — Resend + React Email (server-only): one sender per message, the templates and their copy in both languages (`src/copy/pt-BR.ts` is the structural source). No sender throws, and all no-op without `RESEND_API_KEY`, so callers keep a path that works without e-mail. See its README.
- `packages/jobs` — Inngest client + typed event map; functions live next to the code they run (`apps/web/src/lib/*-jobs.ts`, a package's `src/jobs.ts`) and are served by `apps/web` at `/api/inngest`. `sendEvent` never throws; callers fall back to inline work. Jobs that write to people follow claim-then-send (its README).
- `packages/audit` — append-only `audit_events`, the `access_events` sign-in trail, row versioning, versioned consent terms and acceptances.
- `packages/backup` — nightly logical backups of every `public` table, plus on demand from `/admin/backups`.
- `packages/ai` — chat providers (Anthropic/Gemini/OpenRouter) behind one interface, used by `/admin/insights`; usage feeds the `ai_spend` ledger.
- `packages/fields` — pure validators/formatters/masks (phone, CPF/CNPJ, CEP, currency; persist digits) + the ViaCEP lookup provider.
- `packages/onboarding` — activation state machinery; the steps live in `apps/web/src/lib/onboarding.ts`.
- `packages/content` — `BRAND` (site identity) + the message catalogs `messages/{pt-BR,en}.json`. The official brand art (the SVGs, as delivered) lives in `apps/web/public/brand/`; every raster is derived from the mark by `npm run brand:assets -w @flyee/web`.
- `packages/catalog` — the `flyee.module.json` manifest schema (zod, published as JSON Schema at `/api/cli/schema/module`) and the catalog's version rules, shared by the upload pipeline and the delivery API.
- `docs/` — `PRODUCT.md`, `PLANO-IMPLEMENTACAO.md`, `DEPLOY.md`, `DESIGN.md` (the committed direction), `HOME-COPY.md` (the home copy the product owner delivered), `ASAAS-GO-LIVE.md`, `BILLING.md` (the billing design), `CLI-CONTRACT.md` (the contract the CLI builds against), `BILLING-AUDIT.md` (historical), `SEO.md` and `TRACKING.md` (rewritten in phase 7).
- `attachments/` — input inbox: drop project material here; agents route each file to its canonical home per `attachments/README.md`.

## Golden rules

- **Finish the work you were given.** Carry each task to its end, and diagnose an ordinary obstacle (an error, a timeout, a locked file, a failing tool) and work through it. Stop only where these rules name a stop: the one step a person must take, a secret, a decision that is the operator's, and what a rule protects. Confirmation before a risky or irreversible action still holds. Close with a recap that stands on its own: what you found and what you did.
- **Platform, not product.** Never add CLI, harness or module logic here. The product exists in this repo only as the `/api/cli/*` contract and the module manifest schema.
- **Configurable data, never constants**: prices, plan limits, device ceilings, rate limits, grace windows, guarantee days and trial lengths live in `plans` and `platform_settings`.
- **The free rung is never offered.** No button, price column, badge or copy sells a free plan or a "free account" anywhere (no "Assine grátis", no "Criar conta gratuita"), and public pages never advertise free versions or free samples. The account with no purchase is the by-product of a sign-up that came from content (a video link carrying `origem`) or from the installer's no-login message; inside the member area it is described by what it is ("sem acesso à loja", "versão de entrada"), never as a named plan: the free plan's row in `plans` is the floor every account has, and its name is for the operator console only. `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/copy-rules.test.ts` fails on "grátis", "gratuito", "free" or "sem custo" in anything a visitor or a member reads, the waitlist answer aside ("sem custo extra" is allowed: it speaks of apps joining a paid access).
- **Copy rules** (decided 2026-10-07): no dash (— or –), exclamation mark or emoji in any text a visitor or member reads, in both languages (site, member area, checkout, e-mails, bell, CLI messages, legal texts; © and → stay), and none of the banned words (desbloqueie, potencialize, sem esforço, soluções inovadoras; unlock, elevate, empower, seamless, robust, supercharge, game-changing, "it's not just"). The operator console is exempt. Enforced by `apps/web/src/lib/i18n/copy-rules.test.ts`, pgTAP `0033_copy_rules` and the e2e text check (`.claude/rules/marketing.md`).
- **The member never uses the terminal** (decided 2026-10-08): no text a visitor or member reads tells them to run a command or to open a terminal. It says what to ask their AI. In the member area and the e-mails that is a sentence to copy, ending with the address of `/instalar.md` (`AskAiBlock`, `installGuideUrl`), with the command beside it as a reference (`REFERENCE_COMMAND` in `lib/install-links.ts`); on the site, a terminal frame is labelled as what the AI runs. A command an AI has to run is written in `/instalar.md` (`lib/install-guide.ts`, both languages) the way an AI needs it: `npx --yes`, `--json`, a time limit on what waits for the person, `add` with `--yes` after one plain sentence (the request is the yes, decided 2026-10-21). `lib/install-guide.test.ts` holds the page, the sentences and the reference commands together. The messages the CLI prints (`lib/cli/messages.ts`) speak to whoever runs the command, which is the AI.
- **Honest metrics**: `product_events` records usage, never content, through one allowlist of names and property values; segment, locale and AI tool are stamped from the profile on the server, never trusted from the client.
- Every mutation records an audit event (`recordAudit` in `apps/web/src/lib/audit.ts`). Every table has RLS, and every new migration states its grants explicitly.
- Visual identity changes ONLY in `packages/design-tokens/css/*.css`; run `npm run tokens:generate` and commit `tokens.generated.ts` with it.
- npm workspaces: install dependencies from the root (`npm install`), never inside an app.
- Icons: Phosphor through the tsconfig alias `@/icons/nexture/*` → `src/icons/phosphor/*` (fallback stubs re-export Nexture). App icons are the exception (decided 2026-10-17): an app's tile draws the ORIGINAL Nexture glyph its operator names, through `src/icons/app-glyphs.tsx`, so an app never looks like a control (`.claude/rules/icons.md`).
- **MUI X through its free packages only** (decided 2026-10-14, as MedChina does): no Pro or Premium package and no licence key in any environment. A feature that only a paid package has (pinned columns, row grouping, a range picker, a funnel chart) is built as the platform's own component, never by installing the package. Enforced by `apps/web/src/lib/mui-x-free.test.ts`.
- Fonts: Mulish (`--font-body`), Londrina Solid (`--font-heading`; `font-display` falls back to it) and JetBrains Mono (`--font-mono`). Londrina Solid has two weights, Regular and Black: Black (`font-bold`) for the display scale and headings from 24px up, Regular (`font-normal`) below that.
- The dark band (footer, deep sections, terminal bodies) is `bg-background-deep`, never the dark primary: it has to stay dark under any palette.
- Red is reserved for risk and failure.
- **The yellow is a fill, never a foreground on a light ground** (WCAG 2.2 AA, decided 2026-10-08; it measures 1.5:1 on white). A label or icon on a primary fill is `text-primary-contrast` (the logo's charcoal), never white; the primary as text, link, icon, focus ring or checked control is the ink (`text-primary-ink`, `ring-primary-ink`, `outline-primary-ink`), charcoal in light mode and yellow in dark. Bare `text-primary` belongs only on the deep band and other grounds that are dark in both modes. Enforced by `apps/web/src/lib/palette-contrast.test.ts`; the reasoning and the ratios are in `docs/DESIGN.md`, palette usage.

## Shared Claude/Codex harness

- `CLAUDE.md`, `apps/web/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/*`, `.claude/skills/*` and `.claude/hooks/*` are the canonical shared sources. They are the platform's development harness: nothing in them is distributed to members. Do not maintain a second hand-written Codex copy.
- Codex reads the generated `AGENTS.md` mirror and the generated `.agents/skills/*` bridges. `.codex/config.toml` points its lifecycle hooks at the same implementations under `.claude/hooks/`.
- `PostToolUse` runs `scripts/sync-agent-harness.mjs` after canonical harness edits. `npm run harness:check` and `npm run harness:test` also run in the pre-commit hook.

## Commands (root)

- `npm run dev` / `build` / `start` / `lint` / `lint:fix` / `prettier` — delegate to `apps/web`.
- `npm run typecheck` — `apps/web` with its pinned TypeScript 5.8. Never run a bare root `npx tsc` on apps/web: it picks the hoisted TS 6.
- `npm run test` — the script tests (`test:scripts`), the package tests (`@flyee/ai`, billing, catalog, e-mail) and the web vitest suite. `npm run test:e2e` / `test:a11y` — Playwright against a production build.
- `npm run ci:verify` — everything CI runs: harness checks, MUI class check, typecheck, tests, build.
- `npm run preflight -- --stage waitlist|open [--target preview] [--file <env file>]` — what an environment still lacks for a stage, by name and never by value. Without `--file` it reads `apps/web/.env.local` over `apps/web/.env`, as the app does; with the file `vercel env pull` wrote, a Secret that did not come back is reported as not read (`?`). No network, no database (`docs/DEPLOY.md`, "Roteiro da abertura").
- `node scripts/prune-messages.mjs --check|--write|--list` — message catalogs without unused or missing keys (pt-BR is the reference).
- `npm run test:db:embedded` — migrations + pgTAP on an embedded PostgreSQL 17, no Docker (first run installs it into `.cache/`). `npm run db:start` / `db:stop` / `test:db` — the same through local Supabase (needs Docker). The `db:*:remote` scripts are gated: see "Safety during the transition".
- `npm run db:schema:pull` — regenerate the Drizzle mirror from the migrations.
- `npm run tokens:generate` — regenerate the TS token mirror.

## Platform decisions

- Deploy: Vercel, only through GitHub Actions (`docs/DEPLOY.md`). Database, auth and storage: Supabase (Postgres + RLS). ORM: Drizzle. Email: Resend. Jobs and cron: Inngest. Billing: Asaas for BRL (PIX, card, Asaas issues the NFS-e) and Stripe for USD, routed by the purchase currency. Until Asaas is set up, Stripe charges BRL too (decided 2026-10-12, `BILLING_BRL_PROVIDER=stripe`): no card installments, PIX only on Stripe's own page, the NFS-e issued outside the platform, the CPF/CNPJ still asked in the checkout (`docs/BILLING.md`, "Moeda e provedor").
- Locales: pt-BR (default) and en, hybrid since phase 7.1: the public site lives under `app/[locale]` with next-intl `pathnames` (pt-BR at `/`, English at `/en` with translated paths, both indexed with hreflang), while dashboard, admin, auth and checkout keep the cookie and profile locale.
- Guides are written and travel in each version's package (migration 0030, `docs/CLI-CONTRACT.md` §7), read through `can_read_guide`; the optional video of a guide is an unlisted YouTube video gated by the page and by RLS (`can_watch_lesson`). Meetings use an external link (Zoom/Meet), with registration and click-through recorded on the platform.
- Do not introduce Cloudflare-specific services (Workers, D1, R2, Workers AI).

This repo stays **private**: the UI layer contains commercially licensed code (the Nexture template components).

===== apps/web/CLAUDE.md =====

# flyee.club web (apps/web)

Next.js 15 (App Router) + React 19 — the only app of the flyee.club platform: public site, member dashboard, checkout, admin consoles and the CLI delivery API. See the root `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/PRODUCT.md` and `docs/PLANO-IMPLEMENTACAO.md`.

> The database is the baseline in `packages/db/migrations` (`0000`–`0018`, plus the migrations added since, described in `packages/db/README.md`). Prefer the function name when searching for a rule.

**`apps/web/ARCHITECTURE.md` is the map of how the app works, area by area, with its files, tables and migrations.** Read the section of the area before changing it (the language of a request, the member dashboard, the public site, billing and checkout, the admin consoles and the account, messages and jobs, auth and the CLI delivery API), and update that section in the same change when a mechanism is added or moved.

## Stack and conventions

- **UI**: MUI v9 is the base of the signed-in areas (member dashboard, admin, sign-in, checkout, onboarding, the CLI screens); the public site renders without it ("The public shell" below). Before building a component there, look for a MUI or MUI X equivalent (installed: Data Grid, Charts, Date Pickers, Tree View, Lab). MUI X is the free packages only: what only a Pro or Premium package has is built as our own component, and the platform holds no licence key (root `CLAUDE.md`, golden rules). Icons: **Phosphor** through the `@/icons/nexture/*` tsconfig alias (real adapters plus Nexture fallback stubs, see `src/icons/README.md`); never import an icon library directly. Import the one icon you render; `src/icons/icon-registry.tsx` (icons by NAME, for the dashboard menu and catalog icons) imports the whole set and ships all of it to any client component that imports it.
- **Styling**: MUI theme driven by CSS variables (`hsl(var(--token))`) from `@flyee/design-tokens`. Two stylesheets, both in CSS layers (`theme, base, mui, components, utilities`): `src/style/base.css` is loaded by every page (Tailwind, the tokens, `style/base/elements.css`, the site's motion and its primitives in `style/site/site.css`), and `src/style/app.css` carries the MUI component overrides (`src/style/**`), imported by `components/layout/app-shell.tsx` alone; it starts with `@reference "./base.css"`, so its `@apply` resolves utilities without emitting them a second time. Tailwind 4 for layout utilities, merged with `tailwind-merge`. The primary has two colours beside its three steps: `primary-contrast` (the label on a primary fill) and `primary-ink` (the primary as a foreground on the page); MUI's `contrastText` is the first, and `style/**` overrides with the second wherever MUI would paint text, an outline or a checked control with `palette.primary.main` (`lib/palette-contrast.test.ts`). Run `npm run check:mui-classes` after touching `src/style/**`.
- **Themes**: one locked palette (`theme-yellow`, the yellow of the logo) × light/dark, as classes on `<html>`. The tokens are scoped to those classes, so the root layout renders them on the server (the palette and the default mode) and a script in `<head>` corrects the mode before the first paint for a browser that stored another choice; in the signed-in areas `src/theme/theme-provider.tsx` keeps them in sync afterwards and applies only a palette listed in `THEME_OPTIONS` whatever a browser has stored (the public site has no provider: the script is the whole of its theming). Never leave the classes to a client effect again: until it ran, the page had no palette at all. Fonts: Mulish (`--font-body`), Londrina Solid (`--font-heading`; `font-display` falls back to it) and JetBrains Mono (`--font-mono`, every `<code>`/`<pre>` and `font-mono`). Londrina Solid ships Regular and Black only: MUI `h1`/`h2` and the display scale are Black, `h3`–`h6` and any heading under 24px are Regular (`font-normal`).
- **Forms**: Formik + Yup in the signed-in areas; a public form validates with plain state and the rules of its server action. Semantic data (phone, CPF/CNPJ, CEP, money) uses `components/product/fields/*`, never a raw `TextField`; persist digits, never masks.
- **i18n**: next-intl; every user-facing string goes through messages. Locales `pt-BR` (default) and `en`; catalogs in `packages/content/messages/`. `src/lib/i18n/messages.test.ts` pins key parity, no blank values and identical ICU placeholders. `node scripts/prune-messages.mjs --check` fails on keys no code renders and on keys the code renders that the catalog lacks. Namespaces: `marketing` (public site), `auth`, `product` (member dashboard, billing, settings), `dashboard` (chrome and menu). The home's copy lives in `components/marketing/home-copy/{pt-BR,en}.ts`; `pt-BR.ts` is the structural source of truth (`HomeCopy = typeof homeCopyPtBR`); the text follows `docs/HOME-COPY.md`, the home copy the product owner delivered.
- **Admin copy is hardcoded pt-BR**, outside i18n: the operator surface has one reader. Code comments stay in English; a database value (enum, slug, status) is mapped to a label, never shown raw. `components/data-grid/data-table.tsx` takes its grid chrome from MUI X's own locale pack.
- **Which language a request is in**: `i18n/request.ts` alone decides it. The public site takes the URL (pages under `app/[locale]/`, declared in `src/i18n/routing.ts`; internal links through `LocaleLink`/`localizeHref` with the Portuguese path). Every other area takes the visitor's cookie, else detection at render time, which never switches a crawler and always announces an automatic switch (`ARCHITECTURE.md`, "Which language a request is in").
- **Path alias**: `@/*` → `./src/*`. **Brand**: identity comes from `@flyee/content` (`src/brand.ts` re-exports it); the logo is the single component `src/components/logo/logo.tsx`, which references the official SVGs in `public/brand/` (light-surface and dark-surface files; `tone="contrast"` on the deep band) and never redraws them. The favicons, the square mark and the home-screen tile are generated from the mark: `npm run brand:assets`.
- **Remote data**: `lib/remote-state.ts` (`RemoteState<T>`: idle, loading, success, empty, error). An error is never rendered as empty.

## Rules of the code

Each rule is explained in the section of its area in `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

- **Screens**: a member screen's `page.tsx` reads with the member's session through `lib/member/*` (`getMemberContext()`), and a console's reads through `lib/admin/*` inside `loadConsole()`; both hand a `state` (`ready` | `error` | `unavailable`) to a client view with plain props, so an error is never rendered as empty. Every write goes to the database function that owns the rule: a member's through `lib/member/actions.ts`, a console's through a server action that calls `requireSuperadmin()` again and records an audit event. Reusable product blocks live in `components/product/*`, listed in its `catalog.json`; every zero-data view uses `EmptyState`.
- **Entitlements**: screens branch on `org_entitlements(org)` (`hooks/use-entitlements.ts`, `@flyee/billing/entitlements`), never on plan names or slugs; RLS and the RPCs still refuse what a screen does not offer.
- **FlyeeClub Pro on the click**: a Pro control is never disabled. Without the right it calls `useUpgradePrompt()(feature)` with one of `PRO_FEATURES`, and the server still refuses the action. A Pro area with nothing published says "Em breve".
- **The AI installs**: no screen gives a command as a task. Where something has to be installed, added or connected again, the screen mounts `AskAiBlock`; a new sentence is a key `ask-ai-*` with `{url}`, and the command it leans on has to be in `/instalar.md` (`lib/install-guide.test.ts`).
- **Usage events**: what counts toward a metric is written by the backend with `trackServerEvent`; the browser reports only offers shown and clicked (`trackOffer`). Activation steps are live predicates, never click tracking.
- **The public shell**: no MUI, styling engine, snackbar or form library on a public page (`lib/public-shell.test.ts`, the `[mui-on-public]` lint). Every signed-in segment wraps its children in `components/layout/app-shell.tsx`, a new top-level segment with pages included. A new public page is declared in `src/i18n/routing.ts` (both addresses), enters `src/app/sitemap.ts` when indexed and spreads `publicPageMetadata({ path, locale })` into its `generateMetadata`.
- **A public page arrives complete**: no loading boundary above it (no `app/loading.tsx`, no `<Suspense>` in the root layout), no loader overlay, and what it shows above the fold is decided before the first paint, from `<head>`. Do not add to its cost: no scripted animation, no client component where a server one does, no message a client component does not read, one icon import per icon. Every number on a public page comes from the database.
- **Motion and tracking**: CSS first; GSAP only through `<Parallax>`, on demand, never in admin code; transform and opacity, `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured, nothing runs forever. Site events are declared with `data-track`/`trackAttributes()` and sent by the one listener; never a third tracker, and none on `/admin`.
- **Prices**: every price goes through `formatPrice` (`@flyee/billing/currency`), with no struck-through price and no "from/to" pair (`lib/honest-pricing.test.ts`). Billing webhooks are idempotent (`claim_billing_webhook_event`), and billing notices never throw.
- **Messages**: every message to a member is written in the reader's language, from `lib/messages/bell-copy.ts` or `packages/email/src/copy/*`, never at a call site; a plan is called by `plans.name`. A job that writes to people claims, then sends: a message may be lost, never sent twice. Without `RESEND_API_KEY` nothing breaks. A job missing from `app/api/inngest/route.ts` never runs.
- **Security**: every `/api/cli/*` handler runs inside `runCliRequest` (`lib/cli/gates.ts`). `/admin/insights` runs each statement in a read-only transaction, which is the safety boundary, not the prompt. Support impersonation's write fence is in the database, and a visit ends with `signOut({ scope: "local" })`, never the global default.

## Commands (run from the monorepo root)

- `npm run dev` — dev server. `npm run build` — production build. `npm run typecheck` — TypeScript 5.8 pinned to this app.
- `npm run test:web` — vitest. `npm run test:e2e` / `npm run test:a11y` — Playwright against a production build (`e2e/baseline.spec.ts`).
- `npm run lint:fix` / `npm run prettier` — lint and formatting.

## Watch out

- `src/style/base.css` imports tokens from `@flyee/design-tokens/css/*`; never recreate tokens locally. A rule a public page needs goes in `base.css` (or a file it imports), never in `app.css`, which the public site does not load.
- Deploys go ONLY through GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`: `vercel pull/build/deploy --prebuilt`); the Vercel Git integration stays disconnected. Runbook: `docs/DEPLOY.md`.
- Server-only secrets (`DATABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, provider keys) never reach client components.
- `apps/web/.env` and `apps/web/.env.local` hold production credentials, of the hosted flyee.club project and possibly still of MedChina: never open, print or copy them (root `CLAUDE.md`, "Safety during the transition").

===== .claude/rules/app-ux.md =====

---
paths: ["apps/web/src/app/(dashboard)/**", "apps/web/src/components/product/**"]
---

# Product (authenticated app) UX

- The `product-screen` skill is MANDATORY for any create/edit here — a `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/product-screen-guard.mjs`) loads it automatically; you never wait to be asked.
- **Goal, not table**: design from the user's job and what success looks like. Never default to a CRUD table of rows — that shape is allowed only when the job really is scan/compare/manage many rows.
- **Never a blank screen**: every zero-data view uses `EmptyState` (icon + why + the ONE next action). A brand-new user must find a path to value (the aha moment).
- **Less text on the screens, and no empty space** (the owner's rule of 2026-11-09, brought from ONE): a page, a card or a section opens on its title, and what it is for sits behind the "i" beside it (`description` of `PageHeader` and `SectionTitle`, or an `InfoHint` beside a card's own title until `CardTitle` is packaged; 200 characters at most in both languages, kept by `lib/i18n/hint-budget.test.ts`). In sight stays only state or data (`detail`: what an app or a recipe does, a meeting's text in its console, when the metrics were read) and what must be read before acting (what the AI asks before it installs, what the billing data is used for, values the site shows to anybody). A definition that repeats its title goes (the e-mails card, the caption over the access's list); a row that opens a record shows it by its pointer and hover, never by a sentence; a tile is its icon and its name. A section or list with nothing in it takes a drawing of `@/icons/illustrations` (`EmptyState` `illustration`): the catalog and its filters, the recipes, the news, the meetings and the next ones, the roadmap (one band when every column is empty), the machines, a guide still to come, and the consoles' lists; a state of permission (a guide closed to the plan), of a record that does not exist or of a read that failed keeps its icon.
- **Onboarding never diverts attention**: `/onboarding` and any `SetupWizard` carry nothing that leads away from finishing them (no link to another screen, no "see more", no list of things to explore); each step does its work in place, and what is information for later lives on `/inicio` or its own page. **Prerequisites come first**: whatever a later step cannot be done without (the second factor, a connection, a fact the database checks) is its own step before the first step that needs it.
- **Who does the work, here**: the member's AI runs every flyee command, following `/instalar.md` (the member never uses the terminal), and the platform never runs AI on a member's behalf (the club never spends AI credit for them). So what the product "does alone" in this member area is a rule, a data read or the platform's own job (rotating the token, publishing a version, ringing the bell), said as the platform's or the AI's work, never as a step the member owes; what the member does is confirm in the conversation, approve in the browser, choose and pay.
- **A card asks only for what is still owed**: a request already fulfilled leaves the card's main area, said as done, with doing it again one click away (`QuickActions`, under `template` in `components/product/catalog.json`); what is still owed is one line in the attention colour with its one button. Never hide a right the member must find in plain sight (deleting their data, revoking a machine) in that menu.
- **State in icon, colour and words**: done `success` with a check, under way `warning` with a clock (never the primary yellow, a fill), to look at or act on `accent-3` with an exclamation, failure `error` (kept for failures), information grey; the words say the state too (`StatusChip`; `CardTitle` and `StateLine` under `template`). An act the member must understand is confirmed in an `OutcomeDialog` (template), never in an `Alert` at the top of the page.
- **A Pro feature is never shown disabled**, whatever the playbook says of a module the account does not have: it stays enabled and opens the upgrade prompt on the click (`apps/web/CLAUDE.md`, "FlyeeClub Pro on the click"); a Pro area with nothing published says "Em breve".
- Long setups use `SetupWizard` (progressive disclosure); steps to first result use `OnboardingChecklist` + `@flyee/onboarding` (state only; step definitions live in the project's code).
- **Engagement**: completion drive (`ActivationProgress`) and competence feedback only. Never ship points, badges, leaderboards or streaks — documented failures, and streaks carry regulatory risk.
- MUI v9 + theme tokens only, next-intl for every string, inline form errors near the field, skeletons that reserve space.
- **Semantic fields**: phone, CPF/CNPJ, CEP and money never go in a raw `TextField` — use `components/product/fields/*` (mask + check-digit validation + CEP auto-fill via `@flyee/fields`); persist `onlyDigits()`, never the masked string.

===== .claude/rules/design-tokens.md =====

---
paths: ["packages/design-tokens/**", "apps/web/src/style/**"]
---

# Design tokens

- `packages/design-tokens/css/*.css` is the source of truth for visual identity. `src/tokens.generated.ts` is GENERATED — never edit it manually.
- After any change in `css/*.css`, run `npm run tokens:generate` at the root and include the generated file in the same commit.
- Color values are bare HSL triplets (`191 100% 46%`), consumed via `hsl(var(--token))` in CSS. Keep this format; do not introduce hex/rgb.
- Every color token must exist in light/dark pairs (`:root`/`.dark` in common, `.theme-x`/`.theme-x.dark` in theme files).

===== .claude/rules/icons.md =====

---
paths: ["apps/web/src/icons/**", "apps/web/src/app/**"]
---

# Icon contract

- Pages import icons only as `@/icons/nexture/ni-*` (the alias may be remapped per project to an adapter set — see `apps/web/src/icons/README.md`). Never import an icon library (Phosphor, Lucide, MUI icons for decoration) directly in a page.
- Every icon component implements `NextureIconsProps` (`size`, `variant`, `className`, `oneTone`) and is a default export. The props type and the size helpers live in `src/icons/nexture-icons.ts`, which imports NO icon (every icon file imports it).
- `src/icons/icon-registry.tsx` (`IconMap`, `NextureIcons`) maps names to components and imports the whole set. Use it only where the icon name is data (the dashboard menu, a catalog icon typed by the operator); a client component that imports it ships every icon to the browser.
- Alternative sets live in sibling folders (`src/icons/phosphor/`, ...) with identical file names; gaps are filled by `npm run icons:stubs -w @flyee/web` (fallback re-exports, never overwritten).
- **App icons are the one exception** (decided 2026-10-17): the tile of an app (`components/marketing/app-icon.tsx`) draws the ORIGINAL Nexture glyph by name through `src/icons/app-glyphs.tsx`, which imports `./nexture/*` by relative path, so an app never looks like a control of the interface. A glyph the set lacks is drawn in the Nexture style (24 grid, 1.5 stroke, two tones, outlined and contained) into `src/icons/nexture/`, then gets its Phosphor stub (`icons:stubs`), a line in `icon-registry.tsx` and one in `app-glyphs.tsx`; `src/icons/app-glyphs.test.ts` fails when the two lists drift.
- Adapters import icon libs from their SSR-safe entry (e.g. `@phosphor-icons/react/dist/ssr`) so they work in Server Components.

===== .claude/rules/marketing.md =====

# Marketing layer boundaries

- **One design system.** Every public page (the home, the institutional pages and the campaign pages in `app/[locale]/(funil)/`) composes the primitives in `apps/web/src/components/marketing/`: `Section`/`Container`/`SectionHeader` plus the archetypes listed in `catalog.json`. Never hand-tuned per-page spacing or widths, never a parallel stylesheet vocabulary. The inherited MedChina "Landing DS" was removed on 2026-09-30.
- The `marketing-page` skill is MANDATORY for any create/edit/add-section under `app/[locale]/(marketing)`, `app/[locale]/(funil)` or `components/marketing`. The `PreToolUse` hook (`.claude/hooks/marketing-guard.mjs`) loads it automatically on Write/Edit in all three, and the `PostToolUse` lint (`.claude/hooks/marketing-lint.mjs`) checks every written file there. A file changed by a script bypasses both hooks: load the skill yourself and run the lint on it by hand.
- The committed visual direction lives in `docs/DESIGN.md` and is STRICT: new pages, edits and new sections INHERIT it. Never re-run the direction engine or restyle the UI unless the user explicitly asks for a "redesign". Adding a section triggers a whole-page coherence pass so all sections stay aesthetically aligned.
- **Locales are in the path** (phase 7.1): Portuguese at the root (`/planos`), English under `/en` with translated addresses (`/en/pricing`). Every public page lives under `app/[locale]/` in a folder named after its Portuguese (internal) path, and is declared in `apps/web/src/i18n/routing.ts` (`pathnames`) with both addresses. That declaration is also what makes the middleware treat it as public: there is no separate list of public pages. Only the public site is routed this way; sign-in, the member area, checkout and the admin keep the visitor's cookie/profile language and have no locale in the URL.
- **No MUI on the public site** (the public shell, decided 2026-10-07, `docs/PLANO-IMPLEMENTACAO.md`, "Casca pública"). The root layout mounts no provider; the signed-in areas mount `components/layout/app-shell.tsx` (MUI, its styling engine, every catalog, the snackbars, `style/app.css`) in their own layouts. Nothing a public page reaches imports `@mui/*`, `@emotion/*`, `notistack`, `formik` or `yup`: buttons, fields, checkboxes and notices are the primitives in `components/site/` (styled in `style/site/site.css` with the look MUI had), a disclosure is `<details className="site-disclosure">`, a menu or modal a native `<dialog className="site-drawer">`, a public form validates with plain state and the same rules as its server action. A client component of the public site reads only the `marketing` keys listed in `src/i18n/public-client-messages.ts`, written as literals in its file. `lib/public-shell.test.ts` walks the import graph of the public pages and the marketing lint blocks the import (`[mui-on-public]`). With MUI in the root layout the home scored 55 on a phone.
- Internal links on public surfaces go through `LocaleLink` (`components/marketing/locale-link.tsx`, used by `SiteButton` for an internal `href`) or `localizeHref`: `href` is the internal Portuguese path, the link renders the address of the language being read. Links to `/auth/*` and other non-public routes pass through unchanged and are not prefetched (`leavesPublicSite` in `src/i18n/routing.ts`): they load the other shell.
- An INDEXED page also goes to `apps/web/src/app/sitemap.ts`, which emits it once per language with hreflang alternates. A `noindex` page (the campaign pages in `(funil)`, `/verificar/[ref]`) stays out of the sitemap and is named in its exclusion comment, and so does `/instalar.md`, the Markdown a member's AI reads (`X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, a route handler, not a page). Indexing is decided by `metadata` + `sitemap.ts`, never by the route group.
- `/ajuda` and `/blog` are DB-managed: content is written in `/admin/help` / `/admin/blog` and fetched through `apps/web/src/lib/public-content.ts` (anon client, published rows). An address in a language serves content written in that language, never a fallback; translations are separate rows linked by `translation_group`, each with its own slug. The public catalog (`/catalogo`, `/catalogo/[slug]`, the numbers of the home) reads published modules through `apps/web/src/lib/catalog/public.ts` under the same rule: a module whose name has no English text stays out of the English pages and the English sitemap, and a catalog that could not be read is never shown as an empty one. Markdown renders via `components/marketing/markdown-prose.tsx`. Never interpolate DB content as raw HTML.
- SEO is part of every page, per `docs/SEO.md`: exactly one `<h1>` (the page title: `SectionHeader as="h1"` / `PricingSection headingAs="h1"` when the lead is not a `<Hero>`), a localized title + description via `generateMetadata` that spreads `publicPageMetadata({ path, locale })` from `lib/seo.ts` (canonical, hreflang with `x-default`, Open Graph URL and locale), and structured data through `<JsonLd>` (`components/marketing/json-ld.tsx`), never a hand-written `<script>`. `Organization`/`FAQPage`/`Product` schemas are already emitted by the layout/`Faq`/`PricingSection`; do not duplicate them. Inner pages add `BreadcrumbJsonLd`. A missing page answers a real 404 and a moved one a real redirect: never put a loading boundary (`loading.tsx`, or a `<Suspense>` around the children of a layout) above a public page, because the response would start before `notFound()` or `redirect()` runs and go out as a 200.
- Marketing copy lives in the `marketing` i18n namespace, in BOTH locale files (`pt-BR`, `en`), campaign pages included. No hardcoded strings. The home's structured copy lives in `components/marketing/home-copy/{pt-BR,en}.ts`, with `pt-BR.ts` as the structural source of truth (TypeScript refuses the build when `en.ts` drifts). Emphasis is inline (`**em**`, `__strong__`, `==mark==`, `\n`), rendered by `home-copy/rich.tsx`; never put JSX in a copy file. The home's text follows `docs/HOME-COPY.md`, the copy the product owner delivered (committed as delivered): what it asks and the platform cannot back stays out of the page and goes to the owner as a decision.
- **Blocking on every public page**: exactly one `<h1>`, real `alt` text, no fabricated testimonials, metrics or logos, prices and limits read from data (`plans`), no struck-through price and no "from/to" pair anywhere (a coupon is named beside the price it gives: `priceCondition` on `PricingSection`), no seats counter and no offer deadline on any page (the founders offer that had them left the platform on 2026-10-08), and no claim that the club spends AI credit on the member's behalf.
- **The free rung is never advertised.** No public page or campaign page offers a free plan or a free account, shows a "grátis"/"free" badge on an app, or lists a free column in pricing: the account with no purchase is reached only through content links (`?origem=…&utm_campaign=…`) and the installer's message, and it installs only the entry version of each app (decision of 2026-10-06, `docs/PRODUCT.md`). The one allowed "free" is the waitlist FAQ saying the list itself costs nothing (`lib/i18n/copy-rules.test.ts` fails on any other "grátis", "gratuito", "free", "sem custo", "no cost" or "at no charge"; "sem custo extra", said of apps that join a paid access, is fine).
- **FlyeeClub Pro is never advertised** (decided 2026-10-08, `docs/PRODUCT.md`). The site exists to sell FlyeeClub, the one-time access. No public page or campaign page names FlyeeClub Pro, shows its price or describes a feature only it has (recipes, meetings, proposing and voting, advanced guides, more computers), with or without a lock: the member area offers it, on the click of one of those features. Pricing lists only the plans marked `listed_on_site` in `/admin/billing` (migration 0037), and the only plan on a page is its highlighted card. Once the store is open, every purchase button leads to the sign-up and from it straight to the checkout (`primaryCtaFor` in `lib/launch.ts`), a page with no menu, no footer and no way out but the terms. The legal texts still name both plans, because they are the contract. `lib/i18n/copy-rules.test.ts` and the e2e text check fail on the name.
- **The visitor is never sent to the terminal** (decided 2026-10-08, `docs/PRODUCT.md`, "A IA instala"). The member's AI runs every flyee command, so no public text says "run", "paste in the terminal" or "with one command" as something the person does: it says what to ask their AI ("Peça à sua IA: instale o flyee seguindo flyee.club/instalar.md"). Until the store opens it gives no address (decided 2026-10-12, `invitesToInstall` in `lib/launch.ts`: the waitlist may be live before the installer is on npm), so every public text that names the page has a twin for the waitlist stage, `<key>-waitlist` in the catalog or `<field>Waitlist` in the home copy, that says what the AI does without the address or a command; `lib/install-guide.test.ts` fails on a text without its twin. A `TerminalFrame` shows what the AI runs and its `label` says so ("O que a sua IA roda…"); a command beside a step is a "Comando de referência". A text that names `/instalar.md` names the address of its own language (`/en/install.md` in English), and the commands a page shows are the ones the page gives (`REFERENCE_COMMAND` in `lib/install-links.ts`; `lib/install-guide.test.ts` fails on a drift). "IA de terminal" stays as the name of the kind of AI the first version supports.
- **Copy rules** (the home brief, decided 2026-10-07, `docs/PRODUCT.md`): no dash (— or –), no exclamation mark and no emoji in any visible text, `alt` and `aria-label` included (© and → stay, on purpose), and none of the banned words: desbloqueie, potencialize, sem esforço, soluções inovadoras; unlock, elevate, empower, seamless, robust, supercharge, game-changing, "it's not just". Where a dash would go, write a colon, a comma or a new sentence; separate items with "·"; a missing value hides its line instead of printing a placeholder. The rule covers the member area, the e-mails, the bell and the CLI's messages too; `lib/i18n/copy-rules.test.ts`, pgTAP `0033_copy_rules` and the e2e text check fail when a mark comes back.
- **Colour on text** (WCAG 2.2 AA, `docs/DESIGN.md`, palette usage): the primary is the yellow of the logo, a FILL. It is never the colour of text, a link, an icon or a focus ring on a light ground (1.5:1). A label on a primary fill is `text-primary-contrast`; the primary as a foreground is `text-primary-ink` (charcoal in light mode, yellow in dark); bare `text-primary` only on the deep band. An eyebrow is `<Eyebrow>`, the accent phrase of a headline is `<em>` under the `site-emphasis` class, a tint of the primary is `/20` or more. The accent hues go on icons, bars and fills while the words keep text colours. The shared components follow it; a page must too (`lib/palette-contrast.test.ts` fails otherwise).
- Motion is CSS first: the hero entrance and `Float` are CSS animations, `Reveal` is a CSS transition started by `watchEntry` (one shared IntersectionObserver in `components/marketing/motion.ts`), `CountUp` is a short frame loop. GSAP is loaded by `Parallax` alone, on demand. Never add a scripted timeline or a ScrollTrigger to a page, and never an animation without an end. Transform + opacity only, honoring `prefers-reduced-motion`. Never import GSAP in admin code.
- Site identity (name, tagline, siteUrl, favicons) comes from `apps/web/src/brand.ts`; the logo is the single component `components/logo/logo.tsx`.
- **Measurement is declared, never a new tracker.** A click worth measuring carries `data-track="<event>"` and `data-track-<prop>` attributes (or `trackAttributes()` from `lib/site-events.ts` on a link built in code), a section worth measuring passes `track="<key>"` to `Section` or the component that wraps one, and the one listener in `MarketingAnalytics` reports them to GA4 and the Pixel. The vocabulary is the one in `docs/TRACKING.md` ("Site events"): add to it there before using a new name. Never add PostHog or any other tracker, never write site events to the database, and never read the segment from anywhere but `lib/site-segment.ts`.

===== .claude/rules/web-boundaries.md =====

---
paths: ["apps/web/**"]
---

# apps/web boundaries

- `apps/web` is the only app in this repo. Code shared between the app and tooling lives in `packages/*`.
- Do not redefine theme tokens locally (`--primary`, `--grey-*` etc.) — they come from `@flyee/design-tokens`.
- This repo is the flyee.club PLATFORM. The product (the `npx flyee` CLI, the harness core, the module contents) is a separate project: here, it only exists as the API contract (`/api/cli/*`) and the module manifest schema it consumes. Never add product logic to this repo.

## Where things stand

The database is the baseline in `packages/db/migrations` (`0000` to `0044_cloud_slot`, pgTAP in `packages/db/tests`, see `packages/db/README.md`); new schema work is a new numbered migration on top. The CLI is on npm: the `latest` of `flyee` is 1.2.6 (`npm view flyee dist-tags`, 2026-11-11).

Part of that list was done after it was written (the hosted database, the first apps, the CLI on npm): check an item against the git log before acting on it.
